Male
male
a. and n. (of the sex that begets; the man as distinguished from the woman; rendering Hebrew zakar, Greek arsen)
From the Latin masculus, through Old French masle. Hebrew zakar is from a root meaning to remember or mark — the male is the marked one, and the same root gives the word for a memorial.

Biblical Definition

Male is one of the two terms in which Scripture states what a human being is: “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Genesis 1:27). Three clauses, and they must be held together — humanity is made in God's image, and that humanity exists as male and female. The distinction is creational, deliberate, and prior to the fall, and it is not a defect to be transcended. Our Lord treats the verse as settling the question of marriage: “Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female” (Matthew 19:4), and he goes on to the one flesh of Genesis 2. He appeals not to Mosaic legislation but to the creation, which is why the argument cannot be answered by pointing to changed circumstances. The law also uses the word for what belongs to God: “every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the LORD'S” (Exodus 13:12) — the firstborn male redeemed by a substitute, pointing forward. And Paul states what the gospel does with the distinction: “there is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus” (Galatians 3:28). The context is who may be an heir, and the answer is everyone in Christ, equally.

Webster 1828 Definition

One of the two terms in which Scripture defines humanity: male and female created he them. Christ grounds marriage in that creation; Galatians makes both sexes equal heirs without abolishing the distinction.

expand to see more

MALE, a. [Fr. male; L. masculus.] Pertaining to the sex that procreates young, and applied to animals of all kinds.

2. Denoting the sex which begets, as distinguished from the female, which conceives and bears.

3. In botany, denoting the stamen or stamens.

4. MALE, n. Among animals, one of the sex that begets young.

5. In Scripture, male and female created he them, Gen. 1; every male shall be called holy to the Lord, Luke 2.

Key Scripture

Genesis 1:27 — "So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them."

Matthew 19:4 — "And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female,"

Exodus 13:12 — "That thou shalt set apart unto the LORD all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the LORD'S."

Galatians 3:28 — "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

Modern Corruption

Sex is recast as an identity chosen or felt rather than a creational, embodied, immutable category — and Galatians 3:28 is used to abolish a distinction Christ grounded in the creation.

expand to see more

Genesis 1:27 states that God made humanity male and female, and Christ cites it as decisive. The modern claim that gender is an inner identity detached from embodied sex is therefore not a refinement of the biblical position but a rejection of it. Scripture knows two sexes, given at creation, borne in the body, and not subject to revision; the categories of gender identity and of sex assigned at birth are themselves the corruption of Genesis 1:27, because they relocate the truth about a person from what God made to what a person feels. This must be said with compassion and without retreat: every person who is confused or in distress about this bears the image of God and is owed truth and kindness together, which is precisely what an affirming answer withholds. Galatians 3:28 is enlisted to the same end, and the verse is about inheritance. Paul has been arguing that all who are of faith are children of Abraham and heirs according to the promise, and his point is that Jew and Greek, bond and free, male and female stand on identical ground as heirs. He is not dissolving the categories; he wrote the household instructions of Ephesians 5 and the qualifications of 1 Timothy 3, which assume them throughout.

The principle to recover is that equality and order are not rivals. The same Scripture that makes man and woman equally image-bearers and equally heirs of grace also gives the creational order of headship in marriage and reserves the eldership to qualified men. These are not in competition, any more than the equality of the Father and the Son is disturbed by the Son's glad submission to the Father's will. The world can only conceive of difference as hierarchy of worth; Scripture holds equal worth and ordered roles together, and the household in which both are honoured is the one in which both husband and wife flourish.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew zakar is the male, from a root meaning to mark or remember; neqebah is the female. Greek arsen is male; thelus, female — the pair quoted by Christ from Genesis.

expand to see more

Hebrew zakar (H2145) — male; from a root meaning to mark, to remember.

Hebrew neqebah (H5347) — female; the counterpart term in Genesis 1:27.

Hebrew bekor (H1060) — firstborn; the male opening the womb, claimed by the LORD.

Greek arsen (G730) — male; the word in Matthew 19:4 and Galatians 3:28.

Greek thelus (G2338) — female; paired with arsen in every New Testament citation of Genesis.

Usage

"Of the creation of humanity: male and female created he them (Genesis 1:27)."

"Of Christ grounding marriage in creation: made them at the beginning made them male and female (Matthew 19:4)."

"Of equal heirs in Christ: there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus (Galatians 3:28)."
